PullRequest.Title: session: Improve reference popup placement consistency
PullRequest.Body:
Short reference collections could open below the input pills and immediately show a wide detail card over the list and its actions. This change makes collections prefer above and keeps secondary details beside their row where space allows, using shared ActionWidget behavior rather than feature-specific positioning CSS.

## Changes

- **Consistent collection placement:** add optional `preferredAnchorPosition` to `IActionListOptions` and `IChatDropdownPillOptions`. Chat-input PR, Issue, Reference, Artifact, Customization, Browser, and Subagent collections prefer `ABOVE`, with fallback when space is insufficient. The existing forced `anchorPosition` takes precedence; unrelated dropdown defaults are unchanged.
- **Reveal details on intent:** the initially highlighted row no longer opens a detail card. Pointer movement uses the existing hover delay; deliberate keyboard navigation, Tab, and ArrowRight can reveal details. Row actions and persistent model-picker previews retain their existing behavior.
- **Responsive, row-relative details:** secondary previews use right/left space and can narrow to a readable width before resorting to overlap. Oversized content scrolls, and content growth/collapse recomputes placement without losing keyboard focus.

## Before / after

Matched **headless component** captures: dark theme, three PRs, first row selected, identical 720x800 viewport and trigger position, with the same crop. The before rendering loads the unmodified shared ActionList from base `d0a02edd39b`; the after rendering uses this PR at `c0c074666db`. These are controlled component comparisons, not native-window screenshots.

### Opening the collection

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Opens below; the initial highlight immediately reveals a card that obscures the collection. | Opens above; the initial highlight stays quiet and all rows/actions remain visible. |
| ![Before: collection opens below with an automatic overlapping preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6777f6b9-2a34-4194-aca3-5f4b856fa274) | ![After: collection opens above without an automatic preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5e6a2f4-32a3-48a9-978f-9312ef3e4a7b) |

### Deliberately entering the first item's details with ArrowRight

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The full-width card overlaps the rows even though usable space exists to the left. | The card narrows into that space, stays aligned with its row, and leaves the list and Copy action visible. |
| ![Before: keyboard-invoked detail card overlaps the collection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97ffef33-be3c-49f5-b229-c2b995566049) | ![After: keyboard-invoked detail card fits beside its row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb105f03-ee4c-425d-b478-051fce8fc19b) |

The component theme sweep is available in [Screenshots & Tests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36155006807/job/108143573933).

## Testing

1. In an existing **local** Copilot session, prepare a short collection of three PRs/issues and mixed References. Open each collection: it should prefer above and remain quiet until intentional interaction.
2. Move over a row and wait for the hover delay, then exercise Arrow keys, Tab/Shift+Tab, ArrowRight, and Escape. Verify detail links and Copy/Remove remain reachable and dismissal restores focus.
3. Narrow the window so only a reduced-width card fits to one side. Verify row-relative placement and readable reflow. Also check a trigger near the top, where the collection should fall back below, and an extremely narrow window where overlap is unavoidable.
4. Repeat with long PR/Issue, References, and Artifacts collections. Navigate to lower rows, scroll into and out of details, and expand/collapse a long title by focusing its link. Verify viewport containment, row alignment, and retained focus.

Local validation passed for placement, reveal timing, keyboard traversal, scrolling, content resizing, and existing persistent-preview behavior. Client transpilation/type checking, targeted lint, and ActionWidget/chat-pill/hover tests passed; the resize correction was additionally verified with grow/overflow/shrink regressions and a headless rich-card reproduction. Four local Copilot scenarios were exercised in native Code OSS.

**Limits:** overlap remains possible when neither side meets the readable-width floor. VoiceOver announcements and physical macOS Split View transitions still need manual validation.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Opening a collection eagerly constructed the first tab-through preview; for image entries this also initiated a file read of up to 20 MiB, and for GitHub entries it allocated/rendered the full rich-card DOM before the user requested details.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Collection opening incurred unnecessary filesystem I/O, allocation, and layout work for the initially highlighted item, increasing open latency and resource use even when the user never viewed the preview.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Opening an ActionList now only focuses/highlights the initial row. Rich hover construction and any image file read are deferred until pointer intent or explicit keyboard navigation requests the details.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, ActionListWidget.focus() called _showTabThroughPanelForFocusedItem() after focusing the first row. That helper immediately called _showSubmenuForElement for a first item with tabThroughPanel, which invokes element.hover.content(). Chat dropdown image entries implement content() with createChatPillImagePreview, and that function immediately starts fileService.readFile with a 20 MiB limit; GitHub PR/issue content also builds a multi-element rich preview. The changed deletion at base line 1641 removes this work from popup opening, while the changed keyboard/pointer paths still reveal the panel on deliberate interaction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a chat-input PR, issue, reference, artifact, customization, browser, or subagent collection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Clicking the pill synchronously builds list items, creates and lays out ActionList, computes the preferred/fallback side, and positions the context view before the collection is usable. The diff removes initial rich-preview construction from this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read an image preview file, bounded to 20 MiB, through IFileService.readFile when an image row's hover content is created.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the fix, up to one read on every collection open when the initially focused row was an image; after the diff, zero reads on open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: ActionListWidget.focus invoked _showTabThroughPanelForFocusedItem, which synchronously called the first row's content factory and initiated this read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Before the diff the read started during popup focus even without preview intent; after the diff it is removed from collection-open behavior.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of sections and entries in the opened collection; list-height computation is linear in entries, while width measurement is already capped to a constant width policy at 50 or more items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread popup construction and layout; only one ActionWidget can be visible. No asynchronous fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved collection data is supplied by existing observables. GitHub hover caches and image-preview state are not consulted on open after the change because the first preview is no longer created. Preferred placement is resolved once per ActionList instance and retained across relayouts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the open call path, deleted eager invocation, content factory, and file-read implementation are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Collection sizes vary, but the removed eager file read and rich-DOM creation are directly established. The added preferred-side arithmetic and extra linear height pass are small relative to existing list construction and are not a reportable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Placement adds bounded CPU/layout work, while the same change removes eager preview work from the critical path; the latter was recorded as a regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Deliberately reveal a rich row preview by hover, Tab, ArrowRight, or keyboard navigation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After pointer delay or explicit keyboard intent, _showSubmenuForElement constructs one preview, wraps transient hover content in one DomScrollableElement, measures it, and positions it beside the row. Metadata previews are synchronous DOM work; image content displays a placeholder while its file read completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected image resource through IFileService.readFile with a 20 MiB limit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active selected image preview; no per-collection fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For the initially focused image row, this read began automatically on open; other rows already required navigation or hover.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The placeholder renders synchronously and image availability depends on the read. The diff moves this existing boundary from collection-open time to deliberate preview intent.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One currently selected row and one preview panel. Repeated navigation replaces the prior panel rather than retaining panels for all collection entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one active submenu/preview. Per-panel disposables cancel the prior image read where applicable and disconnect listeners/observers when the panel is cleared.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHub preview caches reuse a DOM root across refreshes; image preview creation is memoized within the entry hover descriptor until disposal. The new scroll wrapper itself is panel-scoped and disposed on navigation or close.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: reveal handlers, panel replacement lifecycle, cache ownership, and file-read call are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rich preview complexity and image size vary, but active cardinality is one and reads are bounded/cancelable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added scroll container and observer are scoped to one requested preview and support viewport containment; they do not scale with total collection size.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize the window or expand/collapse content while a rich preview is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A window resize synchronously recomputes panel geometry; content size changes are observed and coalesced to one layout at the next animation frame. Layout reads the list, row, panel, content, and scrollbar geometry and updates panel width/position/viewport height.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resize-event frequency or content-size changes for one active panel, independent of collection length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active panel. ResizeObserver notifications share a MutableDisposable frame callback, so multiple notifications before that callback coalesce; window resize handling is synchronous but remains one bounded panel layout per event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Geometry is recomputed because viewport and content dimensions are authoritative; observers and resize listeners are removed with the submenu disposable store.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the layout/read-write mechanism and lifecycle; lower for any material latency impact because cardinality is fixed at one.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native resize frequency and device layout cost are unmeasured. The path performs several synchronous geometry reads, but only for one visible preview and does not establish a high-confidence user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The new responsive relayout is bounded, the observer is frame-coalesced, and the available evidence does not show material resize jank.

Scenarios.Scenario: Filter or relayout an open preferred-position ActionList
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Filtering updates visible rows, computes the stable resolved side and available height, lays out the list, then asks ContextView to reposition. The side decision is made only on first layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible and total entry counts; height calculation is linear and existing ActionList rendering/measurement already scales with the same collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-widget UI work with no queue or parallel operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resolved above/below direction and fixed content height are retained for the ActionList lifetime; no cross-open cache is needed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: computeHeight and layout call flow are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large collections could increase list computation generally, but the diff adds only a bounded first-placement calculation plus one linear numeric height pass and does not introduce boundary work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the direction lock avoids repeated flip decisions and added work is not disproportionate to existing list layout.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all eight changed files. No diff-introduced actionable performance issue met the reporting threshold. The change removes an eager first-preview path that could start a bounded 20 MiB image file read and rich-card DOM work on collection open; that regression fix was recorded against introducing commit 4d3755c056420033d92f58157e53e1e5ef3115a7.
